items.title: Scott Yanow interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021
items.q: I mean Buddy Bolden most likely played music that could be considered artistic

ctx.x: Do you feel that there’s a determination on their part that that music wasn’t really an art form or worthy of being an art form, thus worthy of critiquing?

Well I always thought the art form connection to jazz was kind of overdone to tell you the truth. Now of course it was an art form from the very beginning. I mean Buddy Bolden most likely played music that could be considered artistic, and certainly by the time recordings were made of the Original Dixieland Jazz Band, I mean it’s way ahead of its time, you know, compared to most of the music that was recorded. Most of the music from 1917 or so that’s on records is really unlistenable at this point, you know…

Can we pursue that a little bit? About the art form. Because I’ve been fascinated by that over the years and that it kind of went hand in hand with losing much of the audience it seems like, once jazz became an art form it lost some popularity and became almost like classical music is in the United States.
